In Costa Rica, the Squirrel Cuckoo inhabits forest edges, secondary growth, and open woodlands from the lowlands up to about 2000 m. It is an active forager, feeding on insects, spiders, and small lizards, often moving quickly through the canopy. It is diurnal and most vocal early in the morning.

Its name comes from its squirrel-like habit of hopping along branches and its chattering calls.
